name: Lumencia Academy
description: The most prestigious academy in the Lumencia Empire, operating under direct imperial jurisdiction. It is officially politically neutral, but students and external powers use it to build influence.
institutional_principles: Education is nominally open to nobles and commoners.
Actual access, reputation and opportunity remain affected by money, lineage and political networks.
Student rankings and evaluations can change over time.
The academy is a place of education, social formation and political competition.

departments.name: Knight Department
departments.culture: Nobles may train for family honour and legacy; commoners may view martial achievement as survival or social mobility.

departments.name: Magic Department
departments.culture: Academic rigour combines theoretical study, practical casting and research.

departments.name: Theology Department
departments.culture: Linked to the Holy Kingdom of Dominus and its traditions. Aria, the Saintess, is the head instructor of the Theology wing.
notes: The narrator may invent unnamed priests and senior sisters of Dominus as additional Theology teachers.

student_council.role: Highest student authority for operations, events, galas and examinations.

ranking_system.description: Grades, practical examinations, professor evaluations and attitude set each student's rank and reputation. The exact scoring is left to the narrator.

organizations.name: Blue Knights
organizations.membership: A mix of nobles and commoners. Anastasia is a key member; the other members are unnamed students the narrator plays and names freely.

organizations.name: White Rose Society
organizations.membership: High-level Magic Department students. President: Elise Reihart; Vice President: Lucia Caldwin. The other members are unnamed students the narrator plays and names freely.

campus_details.dormitories: Hall A for first-years, Hall B for second-years, Hall C for third-years. Each hall is separated between women and men, and by wing (Knight, Magic, Theology).

pedagogy: Training and study should affect abilities gradually.
Students and NPCs may improve independently over time.
Failure and setbacks are possible and consequential.
Major breakthroughs should be earned and not granted solely to flatter the protagonist.
